newsitem.title: SPAIN: TELEFONICA TO REDUCE CANALSATELITE STAKE.
newsitem.headline: TELEFONICA TO REDUCE CANALSATELITE STAKE.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica has agreed to sell part of its stake in CanalSatelite, a digital television platform that competes with its own Via Digital, the national stock market commission (CNMV) said on Tuesday.

Telefonica, the former state telephone service provider, had taken on 15 percent of CanalSatelite through the purchase this month of a stake in television station Antena 3 and its associated soccer viewing rights firm GMAF.

As part of the negotiated deal, details of which the CNMV published in a statement, Telefonica agreed to sell 7.5 percent of CanalSatelite by October 25 for 1.28 billion pesetas ($8.1 million) and to "remain with 7.5 percent of CanalSatelite without the possibility of influencing its management or its strategic or commercial strategies".
Telefonica also agreed to guarantee the liquidity and value of Antena 3 through the second year of investment to banks BCH and Santander, which also took stakes in the television station and in GMAF.
The CNMV said Telefonica would float Antena 3 on the Madrid bourse, if and when Spanish legislation allowed it.

In the final deal, Telefonica agreed to buy 25 percent of Antena 3 for 26 billion pesetas on August 18 and to purchase 49 percent of Gestora de Medios Audiovisuales Futbol (GMAF) for 18.5 billion pesetas.
On the same date, Santander and BCH agreed to increase their participation in Antena 3 to 21.57 percent and 21.36 percent respectively.
